channel.title: The daily tape · compute.world
channel.description: On the morning of Nvidia's first results without Jensen Huang, Washington changed what a foreign AI data centre can sell. A Commerce Department interim final rule released on 16 November requires a license to ship advanced AI chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Brazil, unless the buyer or its parent is headquartered in the United States and the exporter files monthly reports. It also requires a license for chips headed to any data centre that will supply more than 12 million aggregate TPP of compute to China-headquartered companies, which puts know-your-customer checks on the operator. For the Johor, Singapore and Batam build-outs, the tenant's passport now decides how fast capacity converts. In the US, capital kept moving: OpenAI took 457 MW of AMD MI455X capacity from TensorWave, and Blackstone's listed REIT agreed to buy 75% of two AWS campuses (647 MW) for about $5 billion. List prices held for a seventh day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69.

item.title: Compute brief - 17 November 2026
item.description: On the morning of Nvidia's first results without Jensen Huang, Washington changed what a foreign AI data centre can sell. A Commerce Department interim final rule released on 16 November requires a license to ship advanced AI chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Brazil, unless the buyer or its parent is headquartered in the United States and the exporter files monthly reports. It also requires a license for chips headed to any data centre that will supply more than 12 million aggregate TPP of compute to China-headquartered companies, which puts know-your-customer checks on the operator. For the Johor, Singapore and Batam build-outs, the tenant's passport now decides how fast capacity converts. In the US, capital kept moving: OpenAI took 457 MW of AMD MI455X capacity from TensorWave, and Blackstone's listed REIT agreed to buy 75% of two AWS campuses (647 MW) for about $5 billion. List prices held for a seventh day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69. Countries: Malaysia: New US license requirement for advanced AI chips unless the buyer is US-headquartered (Wire, 16 Nov, confirmed). Singapore: Same BIS license requirement; remote-access control for China-headquartered customers (Wire, 16 Nov, confirmed). Indonesia: Added to the BIS license list with Thailand and Brazil (Wire, 16 Nov, confirmed). United States: OpenAI takes 457 MW of AMD capacity from TensorWave; BXDC buys 75% of 647 MW of AWS campuses for about $5 billion (Wire, 16 Nov, confirmed). Australia: Firmus seeks $3 billion and customer prepayments; 916 MW contracted, 46 MW live (Wire, 16 Nov, single-source). Egypt: Vodafone Egypt, Elsewedy and Cassava JV: 20 MW first, up to 200 MW, $1 billion at full build (Wire, 17 Nov, confirmed).
